prompt:
Create a high-fidelity UI DESIGN COMPARISON BOARD for Jazz Ear Lab V2. This is composition option A, "HARMONIC BOARD". Show TWO faithful browser viewport mockups side by side: a landscape desktop viewport occupying 77% of the board on the left and a narrow portrait mobile viewport on the right. Both show the SAME Progression Recognition question, ready to answer. Small board labels outside frames: A — HARMONIC BOARD, Desktop, Mobile. No device hardware, no perspective, no decorative art.

The provided reference contributes ONLY the existing product's typography (Source Sans 3 humanist sans), near-black navigation, signal yellow #f8d808, cool open background #f5fbfe, white native controls, flat thin gray rules, modest square corners. DO NOT copy its split sidebar layout or large "3 chords" filler. This option's NEW structure is a full-width, integrated music-and-answer sheet. Desktop: existing black brand/navigation header, a compact yellow session band (Progression Recognition, Question 3 / 10, Stop); then a small quiet Ready to answer status and heading "Identify each chord degree". A single large open sheet presents THREE EQUAL CHORD COLUMNS, Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7, each headed with chord symbol around 38px and "4 beats". Beneath each chord are TWO numbered target positions, Note 1 and Note 2, vertically stacked and aligned across all columns, with large accessible WHITE NATIVE SELECTS for answers. Use concrete values: Dm7 Note1 shows b3, Note2 shows 5; G7 Note1 shows 3, Note2 is blank with "Choose degree"; Cmaj7 Note1 shows maj7, Note2 shows 9. Chord columns separated only with fine gray rules; no floating cards or heavy borders. Melody positions and their answer belong in the same sheet. Under sheet: quiet "80 BPM · 2 notes per chord". Bottom action row Replay whole progression (secondary white) on the left and Submit all answers (yellow primary) on the right. Every answer remains simultaneously available, no selected-note editor, no pagination, no invented new behavior.

Mobile must be a real portrait interface in the SAME style, header arranged for narrow width, compact yellow session band. Preserve ALL THREE CHORDS and ALL SIX answer selects on ONE answer surface: stack 3 compact chord rows, and within each row put Note1 and Note2 next to each other. Show enough of the portrait viewport to include the action row at its bottom without tiny type; scale the preview as a whole, not the UI type. Avoid huge typography and duplicate labels. This is an Operate app screen: quiet, precise, highly usable, finished UI with legible actual text. No gradients, shadows, icons masquerading as emoji, dashboard metrics, audio waveforms or commercial copy. The board must convincingly establish a new composition within the supplied identity.
